Markus / Priyom —

I've completed a draft of our responses for the legal/controls sections and attached a PDF for review (SSQ_Answers_v1.pdf). Key highlights and open flags (inline):

- Classification: We propose the attached PII taxonomy mapping (sheet 3 in the Acme template). By default we label any natural person identifiers plus unredacted protected health info and financial account numbers as "sensitive PII".
- Access controls: Engineers on Hosted plan have scoped access to aggregated telemetry only; Dedicated/Private customers can choose admin role scoping. We need Priyom to confirm whether there are exceptions for debugging sessions where raw request bodies are accessible to ops.
- Transfers: We provide regional routing by customer preference; backups may be replicated to a secondary region for resilience with encryption at rest. Need Priyom to confirm KMS key custody and whether we provide customer‑managed keys for Private deployments.
- Retention: We can commit to 30/90/365 tiered retention windows depending on data class — precise log export and deletion runbooks are an open item for procurement wording.

Please review the attached PDF and the inline comments. Priyom, can you attach the updated dataflow diagram and comment on the KMS custody/CMK option?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Data Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Retail — Security questionnaire: PII handling & dataflow

Marissa —

I've gone through the draft and updated the technical sections. See notes below and attached dataflow diagram (dataflow_diagram_v2.png). Summary answers to the open flags: 

1) Raw request access 
- Default: raw request payloads are encrypted at rest and only accessible via a restricted debug workflow. Debug access requires a Just‑In‑Time approval and is logged to the audit trail. Only SREs with a documented incident ticket can access unredacted payloads.

2) KMS custody and customer managed keys (CMK)
- Hosted API: Redwood manages KMS keys (AES‑GCM, KMS hardened) with HSM backing. We provide key rotation and key access logs.
- Dedicated & Private: customers can bring their own KMS/CMK for encryption at rest; in Private deployments the CMK stays in the customer's KMS. We attached flow annotations showing where envelope encryption occurs.

3) Cross‑border processing
- We route inference requests to the region pinned in the customer config. For failover, requests can fall back to a secondary region (customer opt‑in). Backups and analytics exports are limited per contract.

4) Retention and deletion playbook
- We can implement retention tiers per data class; deletion is executed via automated jobs and recorded in an exportable audit log. For regulated exports we provide an export package and certificate of deletion.

I've uploaded the annotated diagram to our shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleSharedDoc and attached the PNG for quick reference. Let me know if you want call notes or a short diagram walk‑through for your architecture team.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Lead, Data Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference

- Redwood_SSQ_Responses_Acme_20261212.pdf (legal + controls responses, includes retention commitments)
- dataflow_diagram_Acme.png (annotated end‑to‑end request and telemetry flow, KMS envelope points)

Topline summary:
- PII classification: we map fields into Non‑PII, PII, Sensitive PII tiers and recommend a 30/90/365 retention model aligned to your risk profile.
- Access controls: only authorized SREs via JIT debug for raw payloads; all accesses are logged with tickets and approvals.
- KMS: Hosted customers use Redwood‑managed HSM‑backed keys; Dedicated/Private customers can supply CMKs retained in their KMS.
- Cross‑border: Region pinning is available; failover is opt‑in and documented in the exhibit.

Next steps: please confirm receipt and whether you need a short walkthrough with your architecture/procurement teams. If the procurement team requests a minor amendment to the DPA (transfer language or retention table), loop in legal and we can produce a tracked redline.

Markus Klein
